topic: market signal review and strategy implications
hypothesis: GitHub popularity is a decoy signal for skills.sh demand, and the real competitive unit is a bundle's mirror network rather than its upstream author: the six established superpowers mirrors hold 19 stars in total yet carry 12.5x the install demand of their own upstream repo (obra/superpowers, 304,600 stars, ranked only 27/60 by demand). Competitor discovery must therefore be built on install-counter streams only (never stars or forks: repo-level Spearman(stars,demand)=0.039 across 60 head repos, and 288,013-star affaan-m/ecc ranks 60/60); demand is read as flow with level treated as tenure rather than size; and the cheapest entry path is publishing a new mirror channel of an already-hot bundle, since a fresh mirror accrues the cohort's full rate immediately (newest established mirror gencraft-labs/skills at level 242,199 still posted delta 1,186 installs in 59 min, same rate as siblings) and closes the level gap in ~512 h (~21 days).
method: read-only re-analysis of cached crawl artifacts + GitHub repo metadata: stars-vs-demand correlation on the 60 head repos, mirror-cohort vs upstream-origin comparison, level-ladder vs rate decomposition, and a unit-labelled concentration table across repo / bundle / stream views. No external actions.

rules.discovery: competitor sets from install-counter streams only; stars/forks excluded as size proxies (rho 0.04)
rules.competitive_unit: the rival is a bundle's mirror network, not its upstream author
rules.size: bundle demand = max/envelope across listings; never sum; label every number with its unit
rules.ranking: rank on flow (installs/hour); read level as tenure/maturity, only legitimate use of level is gap/time-to-parity
rules.entry: publishing a new mirror channel of a hot bundle inherits the cohort rate from day one and reaches level parity in ~3 weeks

falsification: fresh crawl with rho(stars,demand) > 0.3 on repos with >=10 listings and non-zero deltas
the seven ~12-install mirrors do not ramp to cohort rate within 24h (then flow is not inherited and mirror-entry loses its rationale)
origin repo 24h delta exceeds cohort per-listing rate (level ladder is a demand trend, not tenure)
24h-apart crawl shows mirror level gaps narrowing on their own (level is not tenure; envelope rule needs re-derivation)
next_experiment: E75: 24h-apart listing-granularity re-crawl of the 8 established ai-video-generation mirrors plus the 7 ~12-install new mirrors; test ramp rate, empirical time-to-parity, 24h rate parity, and stars-vs-demand on a larger restricted sample
safety: read-only analysis of cached artifacts; exactly one analyze proposal created; no external actions, no posts, no PRs
